scores.reason: Measure type: C-peptide plus total insulin and insulin antibodies (fasting or meal-timed samples). Narrowest population: adults with documented endogenous hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia in whom insulin antibodies are checked. Chain: insulinoma incidence about 1 per 250,000 patient-years (Cryer 2009) x US adults about 260 million = about 1,000 to 1,400 per year; other endogenous hyperinsulinism without gastric surgery (non-insulinoma, IAS, others) assumed to add 1 to 3 times that (assumption, no source) = point estimate about 3,000 per year, range about 1,300 to 10,000. Bin 2 (1,000 to 10,000). Alternative: bin 3 if all adults worked up for suspected hyperinsulinism (assumption, probably 10,000 or more) are counted, which rule 24 says to give as a note only. True IAS cases are far fewer: Japan rate 0.017 per 100,000 (case-report citation) would give at most about 60 per year in the US, and non-Asian rates are lower (Caucasian about 1 case per year in an Italian series). That is bin 1 and is the case count, not the situation count.
sources: PMID 32308449 DOI 10.2147/dmso.s219438 search excerpt only (incidence table)
Annals Clinical Cases DOI 10.7326/aimcc.2023.1485 search excerpt only (Japan 0.017 per 100,000)

scores.reason: Measure: insulin, C-peptide and insulin antibodies (fasting or meal-timed). Cryer 2009 (Endocrine Society, US) recommends in patients suspected of endogenous hyperinsulinism to measure glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, BOHB and drug screen during hypoglycaemia and to 'measure insulin antibodies' (recommendation 2.1, 1|QQQE strategy). Its table gives 'positive antibody' as the insulin autoimmune interpretation, and it says to localise an insulinoma only if antibodies are absent. Population is explicit (adults with hypoglycaemia without diabetes). Not scored 4: the decision named (avoid imaging/surgery) is sequenced after antibody testing, but the text does not say the test must be done first; a reader could argue 4. PEG precipitation is not mentioned in the screened excerpts.
sources: PMID 19088155 DOI 10.1210/jc.2008-1410 (Cryer 2009 Endocrine Society guideline; recommendation text and tables read in a full-text PDF extract via web fetch, excerpt-level, not complete)

scores.reason: Measure: insulin and C-peptide in infants with hypoglycaemia (interference by maternal antibodies). No count of affected infants was found. Chain: US births 3,628,934 (2024, NCHS) ; congenital hyperinsulinism birth prevalence 1 in 17,394 in Western Australia (abstract) gives about 200 infants, and rarer elsewhere (assumed 1 in 50,000 = about 70), so about 70 to 200 infants per year have the hyperinsulinism work-up, plus other infants with a critical sample; infants whose raised insulin is an antibody artefact are a small unsourced fraction. Point estimate about 300 infants per year (assumption), range 50 to 3,000, bin 1 (100 to 1,000), confidence low. Alternative: bin 2 if more than about 1,000 infants a year have a critical sample with a maternal-antibody question; bin 0 if fewer than 100.

scores.reason: Measure: insulin and C-peptide at hypoglycaemia in infants, with PEG precipitation for antibody interference. The Pediatric Endocrine Society 2015 recommendations (US) call for a critical sample with insulin and C-peptide in persistent hypoglycaemia, a broader population that includes this one, but the full text (PMC11891912, text-searched) contains no match for antibod*, maternal or PEG, so the maternal-antibody artefact is not addressed. Rule 14 gives 2.

Measure: stimulated C-peptide (mixed-meal, 2 to 4 h AUC) as a trial endpoint. Situation = patients enrolled per year in US trials with a C-peptide beta-cell endpoint. ClinicalTrials.gov search (T1D, primary outcome C-peptide, start 2023 onward, US site): 18 records, about 12 relevant trials with planned enrolment totalling about 2,040 (e.g. NCT07088068 723, NCT07222332 300, NCT06111586 197, NCT07187531 159) over about 3.5 years, many with sites outside the US. Estimate about 300 to 600 US participants per year (assumption: about half of enrolment is in the US), range 150 to 1,500. Bin 1 (100 to 1,000); the range reaches bin 2, so confidence is low. Not included: routine clinical use (for example label selection, row 29) and trials whose primary outcome field does not say C-peptide.
sources: Endotext NBK326738 (about 50,000 new T1D cases a year, context only) search excerpt

scores.reason: Measure: stimulated C-peptide (MMTT). The 2026 TZIELD US label (BLA 761183, supplement 010) carries an accelerated-approval indication for recently diagnosed Stage 3 T1D 'based on evidence of reduced C-peptide decline', with a primary trial endpoint of C-peptide AUC change, and requires peak C-peptide of 0.2 pmol/mL or more on MMTT for selection. That is regulatory acceptance as a surrogate (accelerated approval), but the C-peptide briefing (C-Path 2025) says no FDA guidance yet qualifies it for traditional approval, and the 2023 FDA draft endpoints guidance excluded early-stage T1D. So 3, not 4.

scores.reason: Measure: C-peptide (fasting) as one input to a remission score; T2D patients considering bariatric surgery. Chain: US bariatric procedures 270,089 (2023, ASMBS) and about 200,667 (2024, ASMBS 2022-2024 volume assessment) ; share with diabetes at baseline about 28 to 37 percent in a US commercial-claims cohort (sleeve 28, bypass 37; adult MarketScan 2000-2020; the exact all-procedure share was not read). Point estimate 200,000 x 0.30 = about 60,000 per year, range about 45,000 (2024 x 0.22) to 100,000 (2023 x 0.37). Bin 3 (10,000 to 100,000). The range touches the 100,000 boundary, so alternative bin 4 if volumes recover to 2023 levels with a 37 percent diabetes share. Counts surgical candidates with T2D, not tests; C-peptide is unreliable in insulin-treated patients and CKD, so the useful subgroup is smaller.

scores.reason: Measure: MMTT C-peptide (beta-cell reserve) around TPIAT. scores.reason: Measure: beta-cell reserve assessment (test not specified in the text I read). PancreasFest 2012 consensus (US meeting; Pancreatology) Guidance Statement 2.4: 'assessment of pancreatic endocrine reserve, and importantly that of functional beta-cell mass, should be performed as part of the evaluation and follow-up for TPIAT.' This recommends the assessment in the TPIAT population explicitly, but names no assay (MMTT C-peptide is one option) and is not a society guideline, so 3 not 4. Alternative 2 if the unnamed test is judged not to cover C-peptide.

scores.reason: Measure: fasting insulin or HOMA-IR (research-only) in women with prior GDM. Narrowest population: women with a GDM history for whom prevention is chosen. Chain: births 3,628,934 (2024) x GDM about 8.0 percent (2023, birth certificates) = about 290,000 new GDM women a year; existing pool about 6 million (assumption: 8.9 percent of women of reproductive age report prior GDM, NHANES 2007-2014, applied to about 65 million women aged 20 to 44, older women not counted; range 5 to 10 million); share evaluated or retested a year about 22 percent (assumption: 67 percent screened within 3 years, NHANES 2007-2012, divided by 3; range 15 to 33 percent) = about 1.3 million. Point estimate about 1.6 million per year, range 1.2 to 3.6 million, bin 5 (over 1,000,000). Confidence low: pool size and share are assumptions. Alternative bin 4 if only newly diagnosed women (about 290,000) are counted or if the retest share is under about 12 percent (rule 24). Note: no insulin test is used in this situation today.

scores.reason: Measure: insulin during post-load or meal tests. Cryer 2009 says an OGTT 'should never be used' for suspected postprandial hypoglycaemia (0 for the OGTT arm of this use case), and recommends a 5-h mixed-meal test with insulin, C-peptide and proinsulin sent only on samples with glucose below 60 mg/dL when Whipple's triad is shown (3 for the meal-test arm, in remarks and tables, not a numbered recommendation); postprandial symptoms without Whipple's triad are called a functional disorder. The decision named is confirming that symptoms coincide with low glucose, which glucose answers; insulin is optional. I scored 2 as the combined reading; see anchor_issues.
sources: PMID 19088155 DOI 10.1210/jc.2008-1410 (Cryer 2009 Endocrine Society guideline; recommendation text and tables read in a full-text PDF extract via web fetch, excerpt-level, not complete)
